hypothesis: Compact turn variant of RFSPGQDVTRSN, whose minimum MSA contact density was 1.0. Tests R/E46, D/K80 and terminal R/E83 anchoring with limited hydrophobicity.
expected_discrimination: Requires joint E46/80–83 engagement; 8A9L separates E46/K80 by 33.7 Å, while 6CU7 buries E46. Prior motif still favored 6CU7, so selectivity is unproven.

hypothesis: Replace the prior turn glycine with threonine to reduce linker freedom and add a possible Q79/T81 hydrogen-bond contact.
expected_discrimination: Test whether a constrained bridge accommodates MSA E46/K80 distances of 6.8–11.1 Å but loses contacts to separated 8A9L anchors and occluded 6CU7 anchors.

hypothesis: Conservative V-to-I variant of the strongest short first-round motif; tests a slightly larger hydrophobic contact at V82 without a hydrophobic run.
expected_discrimination: V82 is exposed in all MSA structures (80.6–119.7 Å²), less exposed in 6CU7 (35.1 Å²); E46 co-engagement is needed to discriminate 8A9L.

hypothesis: F-to-Y substitution preserves the compact turn while testing an additional polar contact near Q79/T81.
expected_discrimination: Combined E46 and Q79/T81 anchoring could penalize distant 8A9L geometry and buried Q79/T81 in 6CU7; local polar binding alone may not discriminate.

hypothesis: Extend the promising short motif with a polar, proline-ended tail to test support near E83/G84 without a long flexible GS linker.
expected_discrimination: Seek retained contacts across all MSA conformers without the 6CU7 contact enrichment seen previously; G84 proximity alone is insufficient for selectivity.

hypothesis: Remove the second basic anchor and introduce an acidic terminus, testing E46/K80 recognition rather than nonspecific attraction to exposed E83.
expected_discrimination: May reduce attraction to control E83, especially highly exposed E83 in 8A9L; MSA compatibility must survive the loss of an E83 salt bridge.

hypothesis: Charge-balanced derivative of RFSPGQDVTRSN; retains the E46-directed basic group and K80-directed acid while replacing the E83-directed arginine.
expected_discrimination: Tests whether lower basicity reduces the original motif's 6CU7 preference; discrimination still requires accessible E46 plus K80 rather than K80 alone.

hypothesis: D-to-E substitution tests longer acidic-side-chain reach toward K80 across the three MSA geometries.
expected_discrimination: Could tolerate MSA E46/K80 variation while requiring both anchors; 8A9L separates them, and 6CU7 exposes little E46 despite similar geometry.

hypothesis: Replace both arginines with histidines to test weaker, pH-dependent acidic-residue anchoring and reduce constitutive positive charge.
expected_discrimination: Potentially reduces control binding driven by exposed glutamates; retain only if all MSA poses engage E46 and K80. Test pH dependence explicitly.

hypothesis: Alternative lysine-based, turn-constrained charge arrangement tests E46/K80/E83 anchoring without reproducing the GS-rich first-round designs.
expected_discrimination: A compact multi-anchor pose could reject 8A9L's distant E46 and 6CU7's occluded V48/Q79; lysine substitutions are exploratory, not predicted improvements.

hypothesis: Polar turn scaffold adds T/N contacts around Q79/T81 while retaining one aromatic group and spaced charged anchors.
expected_discrimination: Seek simultaneous E46 and Q79/T81 contacts: these are accessible in MSA, separated in 8A9L and largely buried in 6CU7. Prior NPG variants lacked selectivity.

hypothesis: Replace a flexible segment of the first-round long turn motif with T/P; test reduced conformational freedom while preserving polar flanks.
expected_discrimination: Constrain bridging within MSA E46/E83 distances of 14.7–20.6 Å rather than 42.8 Å in 8A9L; require no assembly clashes in 6XYO and exclusion of buried 6CU7 anchors.

hypothesis: Short helix-biased alternative places polar and charged groups on a less flexible scaffold; tests E46/K80/E83 contacts without a glycine-rich linker.
expected_discrimination: Compact presentation may favor MSA anchor proximity over 8A9L separation; 6CU7 rejection must come from accessibility, since its distances resemble 6XYO.

hypothesis: Extend the helix-biased alternative with a soluble polar tail to accommodate MSA distance variation and contact Q79/T81.
expected_discrimination: Tests geometry plus accessibility rather than sequence recognition: all receptors share the anchors, but 6CU7 buries Q79/T81 and 8A9L separates E46 from them.

hypothesis: Long, predominantly polar alternative with one proline hinge and balanced side-chain charge; avoids the repeated GS linker of the least-negative first-round design.
expected_discrimination: Could span MSA E46/E83 distances of 14.7–20.6 Å while requiring V48/Q79 access absent in 6CU7; check that flexibility does not permit 8A9L binding or reproduce prior 6XYO assembly clashes.
